correctness.rationale: For D_n=μ^n(0), n≥3, the block form XYXXXYXY with X=D_(n−3) and Y its last-bit flip supplies partners at offsets +4h,+h,−h,−4h,−6h on the five intervals. The first four matches end at a differing final block bit; in the fifth the remaining suffix repeats in full. Opposite-parity positions have LCP at most two since every even-start triple ends in zero while an odd-start triple beginning in zero must be 001 (the source word has no 11). Same-parity LCPs have upper bounds 2r_n(a)+1 and 2r_n(a) after morphing, with the actual suffix lengths giving the sharper fifth piece. The base profile at n=3 matches directly; the resulting upper bounds coincide with the explicit lower bounds for every order. A net occurrence must have length r_n(i)>0 and, away from the left boundary, r_n(i−1)<r_n(i)+1. Applying this criterion gives exactly the five claimed pairs, including the equality at 6h. Independently, direct all-pairs suffix comparisons and direct enumeration of repeated factors with unique extensions matched every case at orders 3 through 7. To replay the finite check, substitute 0→01 and 1→00, compare each suffix with all other suffixes, and tabulate every nonempty substring by its starting positions before checking its left and right extensions. The frozen check_period_net.py was inspected, not run; the frozen log reports orders 3 through 14. Neither finite check is used as the all-order proof.

evidence: The indexed Finding gives all four minimal unique substrings, at 2h−1, 3h−1, 4h−1 and 6h−1, each of length 2h+1, for the same D_n and n≥3.
A substring of a finite word is unique if and only if it contains a minimal unique substring: choose a shortest unique subfactor for necessity and use uniqueness of the subfactor for sufficiency.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: For a suffix starting at i, its shortest unique prefix ends at the first possible endpoint of a minimal unique substring whose start is ≥i. If there is none, the full suffix repeats. Conversely the position of every minimal unique substring is visible at a noninitial net start: whenever r(i)≥r(i−1), the unique factor beginning at i−1 of length r(i−1)+1 has its proper prefix and suffix repeated. Thus the minimal-unique-substring terminology identifies equivalent, not merely nearby, data here.
